transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?
My mind feels foggy all the time now, and I can’t focus or make simple decisions at work. It just feels like my brain is stuck in molasses, and even basic tasks feel completely overwhelming.
In the past two weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or unable to enjoy things you usually like?

Yes, I've been feeling completely down and hopeless, and I've totally lost interest in things I used to love like playing basketball, going to art galleries, and volunteering. This drained, joyless state has been going on constantly for about two months now, not just the last two weeks.
In the past two months, have you also been feeling excessive worry or tension about many different things most days, and is it hard to control that worry?
I don't really worry about a lot of different things. Almost all of my anxiety is focused on how badly I'm doing at work and this constant fear I have about being watched there.

When you feel like you’re being watched at work, do you believe that is definitely true even if other people say there’s no evidence for it, or do you think it might be your mind playing tricks on you?

I believe it is definitely true, and I just can't believe my manager when they say it's just standard security monitoring. It feels completely real to me that corporate is watching me specifically because I've been messing up so much lately. I guess on the rare days when I feel a little bit more like myself, the idea can seem kind of ridiculous, but most of the time I'm convinced.
When you believe your manager or company is watching you, do you ever hear or see things that other people don’t, or have other unusual experiences like messages being sent specifically to you?

No, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and I don't get any kind of secret messages. But I am absolutely convinced that the store's security cameras and even my own phone are being used to watch me specifically. I know corporate is monitoring my every move to catch all my mistakes so they can finally fire me.
Have the beliefs that you are being watched been present only when you feel depressed, or have they continued even during times when your mood feels normal?

No, those thoughts only started after my mood completely crashed about two months ago when the promotion fell through. On the rare days lately when I feel a tiny bit more like my usual self, that feeling of being watched completely eases up or even seems kind of ridiculous.
Have you ever had a time when you felt depressed but the belief that you were being watched was still completely fixed and true, even when your mood improved or felt normal?

No, it doesn't stay fixed like that when my mood improves. On the rare days when I feel a little more like my usual self, that feeling of being watched actually eases up and starts to seem kind of ridiculous to me. It only feels completely real when I'm down.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a 2-month episode of persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia, cognitive slowing/fog, impaired concentration/decision-making, and hopelessness, with mood-congruent persecutory delusional beliefs about being watched at work. The psychotic belief occurs only during the depressive episode and eases when mood improves, supporting a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a primary delusional disorder or nonpsychotic depression.
